# Cyrena.Screens — Screen Share Interop

## Purpose

Browser screen-capture interop for the Cyrena app, packaged as an Extensa extension. Lets a chat pick a screen/window/tab, hold that source alive across multiple captures, and lets the AI call `capture` from any kernel function without juggling tokens. The interop is **kernel-scoped**: one `IScreenInterop` instance per chat, isolated from every other chat. The active source for chat A is invisible to chat B.

## Architectural Model

- **One instance per chat.** `IScreenInterop` is registered as a kernel-singleton in `AssistantPlugin.LoadAsync`. Each chat's kernel builds its own `ScreenInterop` instance with its own active source. Chat A and chat B can share different monitors simultaneously.
- **The interop holds the active source.** Consumers (AI functions, UI components) never pass tokens around. They call `RequestShareAsync()`, `CaptureAsync()`, `StopAsync()` on the interop and the interop figures out which stream to address.
- **State lives in .NET.** Active token, label, surface type, dimensions, browser support flag — all C# fields.
- **JS holds the only real `MediaStream` references**, in a `Map<token, ActiveSource>` in module scope. The .NET instance tells JS which token to capture from and JS does the work.

## Why Per-Kernel, Not Per-Document

The same browser document hosts multiple chats (a `MainLayout` with several `Chat` instances). A single module-scope "current source" would be an implicit mutex: chat A picking a new source would destroy chat B's source. Per-kernel scoping means the JS Map can hold N concurrent streams, one per chat that has an active source.

## Configure-Based Wiring

`IScreenInterop` extends `IDisposable` and requires an explicit `Configure(IJSRuntime)` call. The constraint: `IJSRuntime` is only available inside an active Blazor component lifetime, and kernel services are constructed before any component renders, so the runtime has to be passed in explicitly.

The flow:

1. `AssistantPlugin.LoadAsync(builder)` runs when a kernel is created for a chat. It registers `IScreenInterop` as a singleton in `builder.Services` and adds `ScreenShareTool` as a toolbar component for that chat.
2. When the chat renders, `ScreenShareTool` (a `KernelComponentBase`) is injected with `IScreenInterop` via `[KernelInject]`. On first render, it calls `_screen.Configure(_jsRuntime)`.
3. When the user clicks the share button, the tool calls `_screen.RequestShareAsync()`. The interop holds the resulting token internally.
4. When the AI calls `Functions.ScreenshotAsync()` from chat A, the kernel's `IScreenInterop` is chat A's instance. The capture uses chat A's token, not anyone else's.
5. When the chat's kernel is torn down, the kernel's DI container disposes its `IScreenInterop` instance. `Dispose` releases the JS stream so the browser stops capturing.

## `IScreenInterop` Surface

The interop is now a stateful, event-emitting service. All consumers go through the same instance for a given chat.

### Properties

| Property | Type | Description |
|----------|------|-------------|
| `IsActive` | `bool` | `true` when a source is currently held |
| `IsSupported` | `bool` | `true` when `Configure` has been called AND the browser supports `getDisplayMedia` |
| `ActiveLabel` | `string?` | Display label of the active source (e.g. `"Display 2"`). `null` when not active |
| `ActiveSource` | `ScreenSource` | Classified type. `ScreenSource.None` when not active |
| `ActiveWidth` / `ActiveHeight` | `int` | Dimensions in pixels. 0 when not active |

### Events

| Event | Signature | When it fires |
|-------|-----------|---------------|
| `StateChanged` | `EventHandler?` | After `RequestShareAsync` succeeds, after `StopAsync` releases, after `CaptureAsync` reports `SourceLost = true` |

UI components subscribe in `OnInitialized` and unsubscribe in `Dispose`. Subscribers must not throw — the interop swallows subscriber exceptions to keep the active state authoritative.

### Methods

#### `Configure(IJSRuntime jsRuntime)`

Synchronous. Bind to a runtime. Called by the toolbar component on first render. Resets the support-check cache so the next `RequestShareAsync` re-checks.

#### `IsSupportedAsync()`

Returns `bool`. Queries the browser for `getDisplayMedia` support. Caches the result. Returns `false` when unconfigured.

#### `RequestShareAsync(ScreenPickPreferences? preferences = null)`

Prompts the OS picker. If a source is already held, it is released first (no callback fires for that release). On success, the new token is stored internally and `StateChanged` fires.

Returns `ScreenOpResult` with `Success`, `Cancelled`, `Error` set per outcome.

#### `CaptureAsync()`

Captures one frame from the currently-held source. The stream stays alive. If the source has ended (user revoked via browser chrome), `SourceLost = true` is set, internal state is cleared, and `StateChanged` fires.

Returns `ScreenOpResult` with `DataUrl`, `FileName`, `MimeType`, `Size` on success.

#### `StopAsync()`

Releases the current source. Safe with no source (returns `Success = false`). Fires `StateChanged` if a source was released.

#### `Dispose()`

Runs when the kernel's DI container tears down. Best-effort fire-and-forget release of the JS stream. Clears all state. Subsequent calls are no-ops.

## `ScreenInterop` (internal class)

JS interop implementation, kernel-singleton. Lives in `Cyrena.Screens.Services`.

- One `IJSRuntime? _js` set by `Configure`.
- Tracks active source in `_active`, `_activeLabel`, `_activeDisplaySurface`, `_activeWidth`, `_activeHeight`.
- Tracks browser support in `_browserSupported` / `_supportChecked` so `RequestShareAsync` doesn't re-query JS unnecessarily.
- All `InvokeAsync` calls catch `JSException` and bare `Exception`, returning `ScreenOpResult { Success = false, Error = msg }` instead of letting exceptions escape the interop boundary.
- `RequestShareAsync` releases the prior source before opening the picker. Cancel/dismiss leaves the interop with no active source.
- `CaptureAsync` clears state and fires `StateChanged` when the source was revoked between pick and capture.
- `Dispose` fires a fire-and-forget JS release. The kernel teardown path doesn't await, so this is best-effort; the browser reclaims on page unload regardless.
- The `JsNamespace` constant is `"Cyrena.ScreenShare"`. All calls go through `$"{JsNamespace}.methodName"`.

## `Functions` (internal class)

Kernel functions exposed to the AI as `[KernelFunction]` methods. The class is added to each kernel by `AssistantPlugin.LoadAsync` via `builder.Plugins.AddFromType<Functions>()`.

### `capture` — `ScreenshotAsync()`

1. Returns `ToolResult(false, "...")` if `!_screen.IsActive` — the AI learns to ask the user to share first.
2. Logs "Capturing screen..." via `IChatMessageService.LogInfo`.
3. Calls `_screen.CaptureAsync()`. Returns `ToolResult(false, "...")` on failure, including the `SourceLost` case where the source was revoked.
4. Decodes the data URL (`data:image/png;base64,...`) to bytes, stripping the header.
5. Routes the bytes through `IFileHandlerFactory.SaveAsync(bytes, mimeType, fileName)` so the attachment is persisted alongside other chat files and gets a stable ID. This is the same path used by `Chat.razor.OnFilePasted` for clipboard pastes.
6. Builds a `ChatMessageContent(AuthorRole.User, "")` with the captured frame as its only item. Empty text — the AI reads the image directly.
7. Sets `_its.Input = message; _its.Iterate();` to trigger the inference pipeline.
8. Returns `ToolResult(true, "Captured screenshot.png (12345 bytes)...")`.

Failure modes: data URL undecodable, save throws, save returns null (handler can't process the type). The AI gets a text description of the failure in every case.

## `AssistantPlugin` (internal class)

`IAssistantPlugin` implementation that wires the screen-share feature into each kernel. Per the framework's plugin-loading contract, it runs once per kernel creation in `LoadAsync(builder)`.

```csharp
internal class AssistantPlugin : IAssistantPlugin
{
    public string Id => "cyrena.screens";
    public string[] Modes => [];  // all modes
    public int Priority => 100;
    public bool Required => false;
    public string Title => "Screen Share";

    public Task LoadAsync(CyrenaKernelBuilder builder)
    {
        var info = builder.GetFeatureOption<ConnectionInfo>();
        if (!info.SupportImages)
            return Task.CompletedTask;

        builder.Services.AddSingleton<IScreenInterop, ScreenInterop>();
        builder.AddToolbarComponent<ScreenShareTool>(ToolbarAlignment.End);
        return Task.CompletedTask;
    }
}
```

The `SupportImages` gate prevents the toolbar from showing up for connections that don't accept image content (a text-only model can't do anything useful with a screenshot). The `AddSingleton` call is the per-kernel binding that makes chat A and chat B's `IScreenInterop` independent.

## `ScreensExtension` (the IExtension entry point)

The class is in the project but currently has no work to do — `BuildExtension` just calls `base.BuildExtension(builder)`. The plugin registration is done elsewhere (the host loads `AssistantPlugin` via `builder.AddAssistantPlugin<AssistantPlugin>()` in the host's `BuildExtension`). If the extension needs to register the plugin itself, add the `AddAssistantPlugin` call here.

## Models

### `ScreenSource` (enum)

Classified type of a screen source. JS populates this from `track.getSettings().displaySurface` (Chrome/Edge) or by sniffing the track label (Firefox/Safari). `[JsonStringEnumConverter]` so it round-trips as `"monitor"` / `"window"` / `"browser"` / `"unknown"` / `"none"`.

### `ScreenToken` (readonly record struct)

Opaque string wrapper. `IsEmpty`, `Empty` static, `ToString() => Value`. Implementation-only — consumers never see the token.

### `ScreenPickPreferences`

OS picker hints. `DisplaySurface: string?` and `Audio: bool`. Both optional, `Audio` defaults to false.

### `ScreenOpResult`

Single envelope for all calls. Fields:

- `Success` — the only field the consumer should switch on
- `Token`, `Label`, `DisplaySurface`, `Width`, `Height` — populated on successful picks
- `DataUrl`, `FileName`, `MimeType`, `Size` — populated on successful captures
- `Cancelled` — true when user dismissed the picker
- `SourceLost` — true when the stream has ended (user revoked)
- `Error` — set on any other failure

### Legacy models

`ScreenStreamInfo`, `ScreenSettingsPayload`, `ScreenCaptureResult` exist from the earlier N-streams design. After the per-kernel refactor they're no longer referenced by the contract or implementation but are kept in the file tree for now. Candidates for removal once it's clear the JS side doesn't need them.

## Recommended `ScreenShareTool` Component Lifecycle

```csharp
public partial class ScreenShareTool : KernelComponentBase, IDisposable
{
    [KernelInject] private IScreenInterop _screen { get; set; } = default!;
    [Inject] private IJSRuntime _js { get; set; } = default!;

    protected override void OnInitialized()
    {
        _screen.StateChanged += OnScreenStateChanged;
    }

    protected override async Task OnAfterRenderAsync(bool firstRender)
    {
        if (firstRender)
        {
            _screen.Configure(_js);
            await _screen.IsSupportedAsync();
            StateHasChanged();
        }
    }

    private void OnScreenStateChanged(object? sender, EventArgs e) => InvokeAsync(StateHasChanged);

    public void Dispose()
    {
        _screen.StateChanged -= OnScreenStateChanged;
    }
}
```

The toolbar shows the share button when `IsSupported && !IsActive`, shows the active source label and a stop button when `IsActive`, and is hidden when `!IsSupported`.

## Lifetime Notes

- Streams survive Blazor page navigations that don't unload the document (SPA route change). The Map in JS is the source of truth for what's still alive.
- Streams are reclaimed on full page unload OR when the kernel's `IScreenInterop` is disposed.
- The `Dispose` method does NOT call `ReleaseAsync` — it does a fire-and-forget JS release. The user-facing path is `StopAsync`, called from the toolbar's stop button.

## Multi-Monitor Behavior

The browser's OS picker lists every available display, window, and tab. The user picks one. JS holds one stream for that one source under a fresh token. Two chats picking different monitors work independently. There is no API to "stitch" multiple monitors into one capture in a web app.
